cards.explanation: The answer is False. The kings and merchants weep and mourn over Babylon (Revelation 18:9-11), but that's a different crowd. The voices John hears in heaven are shouting, “Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God!” John says it sounds like the roar of a great multitude.

The reason is that His judgments are true and just. The voices say, “For His judgments are true and just.” That's the reason behind all the shouting, friends. They aren't praising because of a deal or a surprise, but because of who God is and what He has done.

The word is avenged. The voices say, “He has avenged the blood of His servants that was poured out by her hand.” I think this part of the passage is a heavy one, and it's worth a quiet moment, friends. God sees what was done to His servants, and the voices in heaven say He has answered it.

The answer is False. The text says a second time they call out, “Hallelujah! Her smoke rises forever and ever.” One shout wasn't enough for them. I respect that, friends, because I've never stopped at one batch either.
The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne. Then they said, “Amen, Hallelujah!” Down on the ground, and straight into praise, bakers.

The voice from the throne calls all who serve and fear Him. It says, “Praise our God, all you who serve Him, and those who fear Him, small and great alike!” Notice how wide that circle is, friends, small and great alike.

The word is small. The voice calls on those who fear Him, “…small and great alike!” Small and great, together in the same praise. If a stamper from the back of a drawer can be invited, believe me, friends, small counts.

The reason is that the Lord our God the Almighty reigns. The voices cry out, “For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns.” That's their reason for the Hallelujah, bakers. And a roar like many waters and thunder? I think that's a pretty good place to say it.
What has come is the marriage of the Lamb. The voices say, “For the marriage of the Lamb has come…” That's the big news behind the rejoicing, friends. And it's why my ovens never go cold.
The word is ready. The voices say, “…His bride has made herself ready.” That's why I help bakers get ready and don't do it for them, friends. Nobody can take a bath for you either.

The fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints. The text says, “For the fine linen she wears is the righteous acts of the saints.” So the bright, pure clothing stands for what the saints have done. It's good to see a verse that explains its own picture, friends.

Those who are invited to the marriage supper are the blessed ones. The angel tells John to write, “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” The blessing goes to the invited, friends. I know that feeling well, and I'd tell you all about it, but I'm trying to keep this short.

The answer is True. After telling John to write, the angel says, “These are the true words of God.” That puts a seal on the blessing about the supper, friends. When the words are true, I don't need to add anything fancy.
The answer is False. John falls at the angel's feet, and the angel says, “Do not do that!” He stops it on the spot, bakers. If I tried that, I'd be stopped by my own mustache.

The angel calls himself a fellow servant. He says, “I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers who rely on the testimony of Jesus.” He puts himself right next to John. It's hard to get humbler than that, friends.
The angel tells John to worship God. He says, “Worship God!” John gets pointed to the right One, friends. Every time I hear that line, I put my mustache down and listen.
